notes: Overall a solid implementation with good separation of concerns and clean TypeScript. Specific issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - main.ts directly calls userService.getById() and taskService.getById() from within the NotificationService wiring context, passing these as callback closures into NotificationService. This is a subtle but real violation of Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) — the NotificationService is effectively querying TaskService and UserService data through injected function references, bypassing the event bus. The callbacks are just thin wrappers around direct service method calls, which circumvents the spirit of the rule even if it avoids direct import coupling. (2) CONSTRAINT VIOLATION - The comment.added event payload deliberately sends empty strings for taskTitle and authorName ('will be enriched by subscribers'), meaning the event bus payload is intentionally incomplete and relies on out-of-band lookups; this undermines the event-driven contract. (3) Status transition enforces one-step-at-a-time (newIndex !== currentIndex + 1), which is stricter than 'forward-only' — going from todo directly to done is rejected, which may or may not match intent but is a reasonable interpretation. (4) GET /tasks requires projectId query param with no fallback for listing all tasks without a filter. (5) Error handling uniformly returns 400 for all errors (not found → should be 404, validation → 400, conflicts → 409). (6) CommentService sends empty-string fields in event payload rather than enriching at publish time using data it has (it has taskId and authorId but not title/name — acceptable, but the empty string sentinel is a code smell). (7) NotificationService.wireSubscriptions() is a manual wiring step that could be forgotten. (8) 204 responses send an empty JSON object {} instead of no body. (9) Demo and main.ts duplicate wiring logic. (10) The Router correctly centralizes all HTTP handling. The event bus implementation is clean and correct. Each service owns its own Map store exclusively.
